properties.description:
* WHAT...Life-threatening rip current.

* WHERE...Beaches along the northwest to northeast coastline of
Puerto Rico, including beaches in Aguada and Rincon.

* WHEN...Through late Wednesday morning.

* IMPACTS...Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water, where it becomes difficult to
return to safety.
properties.instruction:
There is a high risk of rip currents.

Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as groins, jetties
and piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

If you become caught in a rip current, yell for help. Remain
calm, do not exhaust yourself and stay afloat while waiting for
help. If you have to swim out of a rip current, swim parallel to
shore and back toward the beach when possible. Do not attempt to
swim directly against a rip current as you will tire quickly.

properties.headline: Beach Hazards Statement issued November 17 at 12:26PM PST until November 18 at 4:00PM PST by NWS San Francisco CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Beach Hazards Statement, An increased risk for
sneaker waves and strong rip currents with breaking waves of
12 to 17 ft. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, Up to 1.3 ft of inundation
above ground level is likely in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal
waterways. For the High Surf Advisory, Large breaking waves of
15 to 18 ft along the coast from Wednesday afternoon through Thursday
afternoon.

* WHERE...San Francisco County.

* WHEN...For the Beach Hazards Statement, through Wednesday
afternoon. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 5 AM Wednesday
to 10 AM PST Thursday. For the High Surf Advisory, from 4 PM
Wednesday to 4 PM PST Thursday.

* IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying
infrastructure, isolated road closures, and coastal erosion.
Rising tides will bring water and waves farther up the beach
than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal
areas. Large breaking waves can overpower swimmers, pulling
people into the sea from beaches, jetties, and rocks resulting
in significant physical injury and increasing the risk of
drowning. Waves can sweep across the shoreline without
warning, pulling people into the sea from beaches, jetties,
and rocks.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...At the San Francisco tidal gauge, high
tide is expected to be 1.3 ft above normal (7.1 ft MLLW) at 6:53
AM Wednesday. These predictions include up to 1.3 ft of surge
that will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding threat. High
tide varies up to 90 minutes earlier or later along the Pacific
Coast and through the San Francisco Bay, respectively.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Swimmers should remain out of the water due to dangerous surf
conditions.

Stay off of jetties, piers, rocks, and other waterside
infrastructure. Remain out of the water to avoid hazardous surf
and NEVER turn your back on the ocean. Monitor local weather,
surf and tide forecasts at www.weather.gov/mtr.

properties.description:
FFWFGZ

The National Weather Service in Flagstaff has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Coconino County in north central Arizona...
Yavapai County in west central Arizona...

* Until 600 PM MST.

* At 100 PM MST, River gages in Munds Canyon indicated over 3 feet of
rises and levels were still rising. This water will the work
through the Munds Park area and into Oak Creek this afternoon.
Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to begin shortly.

SOURCE...Radar and river gage indicated.

normally dry washes, urban areas, highways, streets and
underpasses.

Sedona, Munds Park, Indian Gardens, Uptown Sedona, Red Rock State
Park and Cathedral Rock.

This includes the following highways...
Interstate 17 between mile markers 318 and 323. State Route 179
between mile markers 311 and 313. State Route 89A between mile
markers 374 and 379.

This includes the following swimming holes...
Midgely Bridge, Buddha Beach "Red Rock Crossing" and Crescent Moon
Ranch.

This includes the following creeks, washes and rivers...
Oak Creek, Turkey Creek and Dry Beaver Creek.

Flooding of washes and creeks will occur, some dirt roads will become
muddy and impassable. Paved roads and underpasses could become
flooded as well.

or pushing into the dunes on South Padre Island. Vehicles,

erosion is expected. Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions

best swimmers away from shore into deeper water.

at 1105 PM tonight and again at 1049 PM Thursday night.
properties.instruction:

closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

dangerous surf conditions.

Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

properties.description:
* WHAT...For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 5
to 11 feet in the surf zone. For the High Rip Current Risk,
dangerous rip currents.

* WHERE...Coastal Volusia, Coastal Indian River, Coastal Saint
Lucie, Coastal Martin, Mainland Northern Brevard, Northern
Brevard Barrier Islands, Mainland Southern Brevard and
Southern Brevard Barrier Islands Counties.

* WHEN...For the High Surf Advisory, until 7 AM EST Friday. For
the High Rip Current Risk, through Thursday evening.

* IMPACTS...Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and
localized beach erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the best
swimmers away from shore into deeper water.
properties.instruction:
High surf will affect the beaches in the advisory area, producing
localized beach erosion and dangerous swimming conditions.
Swimmers should remain out of the water due to large breaking
waves and dangerous surf conditions.

Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as jetties and
piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

Entering the surf is strongly discouraged. If caught in a rip
current, relax and float. Don't swim against the current. If
able, swim in a direction following the shoreline. If unable to
escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.

properties.headline: Winter Storm Warning issued November 17 at 6:17AM PST until November 19 at 1:00AM PST by NWS Eureka CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Heavy snow expected. Total snow accumulations between 8 and
12 inches possible above 4000 ft, with 3 to 5 inches possible down
to 3500 ft.  Winds gusting as high as 50 mph.

* WHERE...Northeastern Trinity and Southern Trinity. This includes
the higher passes on Highway 3 and 36.

* WHEN...From 7 PM this evening to 1 AM PST Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be very difficult to impossible. Tire chains
may be necessary if travelling through mountain passes. Roads, and
especially bridges and overpasses, will likely become slick and
hazardous.
properties.instruction:
If you must travel, keep an extra flashlight, food, and water in your
vehicle in case of an emergency. The latest road conditions for the
state you are calling from can be obtained by calling 5 1 1.

properties.headline: Rip Current Statement issued November 17 at 8:09AM EST until November 19 at 7:00PM EST by NWS Miami FL
properties.description:
* WHAT...Dangerous rip currents.

* WHERE...Coastal Miami Dade County.

* WHEN...Through Thursday evening.

* IMPACTS...Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water.
properties.instruction:
Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

properties.description:

to 12 feet in the surf zone. For the High Rip Current Risk,
dangerous rip currents.

properties.headline: Flood Watch issued November 17 at 8:07AM EST until November 19 at 7:00PM EST by NWS Miami FL
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flash flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...A portion of southeast Florida, including the following
areas, Coastal Broward County, Coastal Miami Dade County, Coastal
Palm Beach County, Far South Miami-Dade County, Inland Broward
County, Inland Miami-Dade County, Inland Palm Beach County, Metro
Broward County, Metro Palm Beach County and Metropolitan Miami
Dade.

* WHEN...From 1 PM EST this afternoon through Thursday evening.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.
Flooding may occur in poor drainage and urban areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Several rounds of storms may produce rainfall amounts of 2 to 4
inches through late Thursday. Higher amounts of 6 to 8 inches
with locally isolated amounts over 10 inches may be possible.
Heavy rainfall rates of 1 to 2 inches per hour may observed with
some of these storms.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be prepared to take action
should Flash Flood Warnings be issued.

properties.headline: High Wind Warning issued November 17 at 4:01AM AKST until November 17 at 12:00PM AKST by NWS Anchorage AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...Southwest winds 45 to 60 mph with gusts as high as 80 mph.
Strongest winds are expected in Adak.

* WHERE...Atka and Adak.

* WHEN...Until noon AKST today.

* IMPACTS...High winds may move loose debris, damage property, and
cause power outages. Travel will be difficult.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The strongest winds will be over Adak, with
wind gusts as high as 80 mph, with Atka winds expected to see gusts
to 60 mph. Winds will begin to diminish later this morning and
remain gusty through Wednesday.
properties.instruction:
People are urged to secure loose objects that could be blown around
or damaged by the wind. Prepare for the possibility of widespread
power outages. Use caution if you must drive.
